plates.quality_reason: Flow-first: a teach diagram, chart, counter or timeline is a £0 code graphic. No Flow mint.
plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, the 3-era timeline completes: 1011–1021 AD (Ibn al-Haytham in Cairo uses the pinhole camera obscura in his Book of Optics to refute Greek extramission eye-beams and prove light enters the eye) · 1604 & 1619 (Johannes Kepler proves the cornea and lens project an inverted image onto the retina and explains concave and convex spectacles, and Christoph Scheiner demonstrates the upside-down flame on a peeled ox eye) · 1801 & 1862–1864 (Thomas Young at the Royal Society proves lens accommodation and discovers astigmatism, and Franciscus Donders and Herman Snellen in Utrecht standardize refractive errors and the 20/20 eye chart).

teach_overlay.scale: from five oil lamps outside a darkened room in medieval Cairo to a peeled ox eye and the big letter E on an optician's wall, scientists unlocked how two spheres of jelly let us see the universe
